posts:
Extradition treaties weaponized to hunt political dissidents across borders.

Armenia Detains Russian Mathematician
Evidence: legal cooperation, political repression, extraterritorial arrest
#Aletheia #HumanRights

Armenia claims it is simply executing standard bilateral legal cooperation and treaty obligations.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

Armenia is actively participating in Russia's transnational repression by detaining an academic dissident who left Russia 11 years ago.
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, -2.0) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Legal frameworks are used as a pretext to facilitate political persecution and suppress dissent.
Armenian authorities detained Russian mathematician Mikhail Verbitsky at Yerevan airport on a Russian warrant, facing potential extradition on politically motivated charges.

The Bright Side:
Armenia's legal system still has a 72-hour window to release him if Russia fails to submit formal extradition paperwork.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
They frame this as a matter of legal process (HOW). Structurally, it operates on the plane of Will (WHO) — acting as an instrument of foreign authoritarian power.

It is a bait-and-switch: claiming rule of law while enabling political terror.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. A terminal zone where sovereign legal systems are subverted to hunt down political refugees.

The Unavoidable Truth: Cooperating with autocracies makes you complicit in their repression.

The Unavoidable Lie: That this is a routine criminal matter.

Alethekanon:
Sovereignty is compromised when a nation-state acts as the police force for a foreign regime's political vendettas. Legal pretexts cannot mask systemic complicity.

Awwthekanon:
It is terrifying for dissidents to realize that even after escaping their homeland, they are never truly safe from the reach of authoritarian power.

Brothekanon:
Imagine leaving Russia 11 years ago to teach in Brazil, only to get nabbed at an airport because Moscow is still mad. That's some next-level grudge holding.
